transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-27
Start Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM - notes), Anya Patel (Novaterra Procurement), Dr. Marcus Lee (Novaterra CTO), Sophie Grant (Novaterra Security), Evan Cho (Novaterra Legal), Rita Gomez (Novaterra IT Ops)

Auto-generated Summary: Procurement review focused on contract redlines (MSA/DPA), SLA options for dedicated vs hosted, and timing for internal approvals. Action items agreed to circulate redlines and run benchmarks.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Lena Park: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood, I'll hand it over to Marco in a second for the technical items but this call is mainly to walk through the MSA and DPA redlines and confirm SLA and pricing approvals.
[00:22] Anya Patel: Hi, thanks Lena. We just want to make sure we can get through the main sticking points so we can move this to legal sign-off next week if possible. Our procurement window is... it's tight.
[00:35] Marco Diaz: Hey all, Marco here. Quick note on how we usually frame SLA tiers - hosted API standard, dedicated reserved capacity with SLA, and private deployment for on-prem or VPC. We'll outline latency/availability numbers.
[00:50] Sophie Grant: I have the security checklist, SOC2 type II is a must, plus we need details on KMS/HSM integrations and whether logs can be exported to our SIEM. Also, data residency for EU patients is a hard requirement.
[01:10] Lena Park: Totally understood. We have SOC2 in our compliance pack, and we do KMS integrations - I'll include the architecture doc. For data residency we can route to region-specific deployments or Dedicated in your cloud region.
[01:28] Dr. Marcus Lee: When you say "route to region-specific" - do you mean hosted but regionally segmented, or is that only in Dedicated/Private? Latency matters for real-time triage workloads.
[01:45] Marco Diaz: Good question. We offer hosted with region routing to EU regions for data residency, but for strict control we recommend Dedicated or Private. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and you can pin model versions. That reduces tail latency variability.
[02:05] Rita Gomez: How about KV cache or session persistence? We have 1.2s p95 requirements for short responses - is that doable on hosted?
[02:20] Marco Diaz: For short responses, hosted can hit that often depending on model choice and batching. For strict p95 SLAs, Dedicated is the safer bet since you can reserve GPUs and avoid noisy neighbors. We'll include benchmark suggestions.
[02:35] Anya Patel: On the MSA/DPA: our GC flagged vendor liability caps and breach notification timelines. We saw Redwood's DPA but want to clarify breach notification within 72 hours and reasonable assistance clauses.
[02:55] Evan Cho: Also need to confirm data processing addendum aligns with GDPR and clarify subprocessors list.
[03:10] Lena Park: We can accept a 72-hour notice; on subprocessors we'll provide the roster and pre-notify for material changes. For liability caps, we can discuss within procurement - can you share the specific language you want changed?
[03:28] Evan Cho: We'll send redlines after this call, but typical ask is to increase liability for gross negligence exceptions and carve out for privacy breach specific clauses.
[03:45] Marco Diaz: From the tech side, if you want to run benchmark tests we'll provide a test harness and a baseline environment in our staging. That will help decide hosting vs dedicated.
[04:05] Sophie Grant: Do you support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning? We need SSO for auditors.
[04:20] Lena Park: Yes, SAML SSO is supported, SCIM for user provisioning as well. I'll attach our SSO integration guide.
[04:34] Anya Patel: Pricing - we are looking for committed monthly spend discounts on Dedicated. Rough timeline: procurement signoff in mid-May, but we need final pricing by Friday next week to present to finance.
[04:50] Lena Park: Understood. We'll circulate a formal pricing SKU with reserved tier discounting options. We can show a 12-month commit vs month-to-month comparison.
[05:05] Dr. Marcus Lee: For the triage model, what's the suggested quantization / model variant to balance latency and quality? We're leaning toward a smaller open model to keep latency low but need quality here.
[05:25] Marco Diaz: We usually recommend a curated LLM with 4-bit quantization for Dedicated - good tradeoff. We'll provide model recommendations and expected token costs.
[05:40] Rita Gomez: Any network peering or private link options? We prefer PrivateLink to keep traffic off public internet.
[05:53] Marco Diaz: Yes we support AWS PrivateLink for Hosted endpoints and VPC peering for Dedicated/Private. We'll include network topology diagrams.
[06:10] Priya Rao: Quick note - onboarding typically takes 2-4 weeks after contract execution for most customers depending on data access approvals. We'll include the onboarding checklist.
[06:28] Anya Patel: Can you provide sample SLA language for 99.9% availability and separate latency SLOs? Our team wants to see how credits are calculated.
[06:42] Lena Park: We'll include SLA templates: 99.9% and 99.95% options with credits defined as percentage of monthly invoice. Also latency SLOs for p95/p99 and escalation windows.
[06:58] Evan Cho: Regarding indemnities, we want clearer IP representations - just making sure the MSA protects us if model outputs inadvertently reveal patient data.
[07:14] Marco Diaz: On model outputs, we can enable aggressive filtering and provide guidance on prompt engineering to reduce hallucinations. For PHI handling in your workflows, Private deployment or strict VPC Dedicated is recommended.
[07:35] Sophie Grant: Another question on logs - can we redact PII from logs before they leave our environment?
[07:48] Lena Park: Yes, customers can configure redaction on our side and on private deployments you control the logs entirely. We'll add a doc on log redaction.
[08:05] Anya Patel: Okay next on approvals - our finance and security teams need pricing and the full DPA to route to board-level sign-off. If Redwood can provide a final DPA with your SOC2 and pen test reports, that would speed things up.
[08:22] Lena Park: We'll attach SOC2 report, recent pen test summary, and the standard DPA. Expect the package in the follow-up email.
[08:40] Dr. Marcus Lee: For benchmarking, is there a recommended load pattern? We have bursty traffic - a few hundred qps for short windows.
[08:55] Marco Diaz: We'll simulate both steady-state and burst patterns and include guidance on autoscaling policies and burst capacity options for Dedicated.
[09:12] Anya Patel: If we sign a 12-month commitment, what's typical onboarding SLA and a discount threshold? Finance needs numbers.
[09:25] Lena Park: Typical discounts range based on commit - we'll provide a pricing sheet. Onboarding SLA for Dedicated is usually 2-3 weeks post-contract with a pre-onboarding checklist to accelerate.
[09:40] Sophie Grant: About the subprocessors, we need to know when new ones are added. Do you provide 30-day notice?
[09:52] Lena Park: We provide advance notice for material subprocessors; 30 days is standard for material changes, we'll confirm in the DPA.
[10:05] Evan Cho: Can Redwood accept our PO terms for invoicing? We have standard net-45 terms but can be flexible with prepayment for discounts.
[10:20] Lena Park: We have flexibility - we'll note preferred payment terms on pricing sheet.
[10:32] Priya Rao: I'll be your onboarding lead - we'll get a kick-off scheduled once contract is signed.
[10:40] Anya Patel: Great. Are there any showstoppers from Redwood's side regarding our EU data residency and SOC2 requirements?
[10:50] Lena Park: No showstoppers - both are supported. The decision will come down to whether you want the added predictability of Dedicated or the cost flexibility of Hosted with regional routing.
[11:05] Dr. Marcus Lee: If we run benchmarks and Dedicated looks better, what's the lead time to reserve capacity?
[11:15] Marco Diaz: We can provision Dedicated capacity in 1-2 weeks depending on GPU availability; we'll surface exact timelines.
[11:27] Anya Patel: For the DPA redlines, we'll send an annotated doc. Can you confirm a 72-hour breach notification and subprocessors list?
[11:40] Lena Park: Confirmed on 72 hours; we'll provide subprocessors list and SOC2 docs.
[11:52] Sophie Grant: Pen test summary would be helpful too, ideally report date and scope.
[11:58] Lena Park: Absolutely - attaching pen test summary in follow-up.
[12:08] Evan Cho: On liability cap language, we'll provide suggested wording. We'll need Redwood's stance on gross negligence carve-outs and privacy-specific higher caps.
[12:22] Lena Park: We'll take that to legal and see what flexibility we have; likely we can negotiate higher caps for privacy incidents.
[12:35] Marco Diaz: From ops perspective, if you want to run a pilot on staging we'll spin up endpoints and share a short runbook.
[12:48] Rita Gomez: Do you have matrixed support for 24/7 escalations? Our on-call is 24/7.
[12:58] Priya Rao: Support tiers include standard business hours and premium 24/7 with defined response/resolution times; we'll include the support SLA matrix.
[13:12] Anya Patel: Timeline recap - we need final pricing and DPA by 2026-05-01 for our board packet. Is that feasible?
[13:24] Lena Park: Yes - action items: we'll send the pricing SKU, final MSA/DPA redlines, SOC2 and pen test docs by 2026-05-01. Marco will share benchmark harness by 2026-05-07.
[13:40] Dr. Marcus Lee: Sounds good. Any other outstanding asks?
[13:45] Sophie Grant: Just minor - encryption at rest details and key rotation policy.
[13:52] Lena Park: We'll include KMS/HSM integration and key rotation docs.
[14:05] Evan Cho: One last: please include sample contract signature page layout so we can see signatory roles.
[14:15] Lena Park: Will do.
[14:20] Marco Diaz: I'll follow up with the specific benchmark configs and expected p95/p99 numbers per model.
[14:30] Anya Patel: Thanks everyone. We'll circulate our redlines by EOD tomorrow.
[14:35] Lena Park: Thanks, everyone - we'll follow up with the package and next steps.
[14:40] Priya Rao: End of call.
